entries.title: Zechariah 6:1 "I lifted up my eyes again and looked"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:1 "I lifted up my eyes again and looked" This is a literary formula to introduce another vision. See note at Zech. 1:8.

▣ "four chariots" The number four (BDB 916) is often used as a symbol of

  1. the whole world (or known world, cf. Daniel 2,7)
  2. the universe (cf. Dan. 8:8; 11:4; Zech. 6:5
  3. see John J. Davis, Biblical Numerology, pp. 122-123; Encyclopedia Judaica, vol. 12, pp. 1255-1259; or Milton S. Terry, Biblical Hermeneutics, p. 382).
    1. four horsemen, Zech. 1:8
    2. four horns/four craftsmen, Zech. 1:18,20
    3. four winds of heaven, Zech. 2:10
    4. four chariots, Zech. 6:1
    5. four spirits (or "winds," like Zech. 2:10) of heaven, Zech. 6:5

"Chariots" (BDB 939) were war machines, the fastest and deadliest of the day. Therefore, they are used as imagery for YHWH equipping Cyrus II's army to destroy Babylon.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #2

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARIOTS

▣ "two mountains" The term "mountain" (BDB 249) is used as imagery several times in Zechariah.

  1. Zech. 4:7, the problems facing Zerubbabel in rebuilding the temple
  2. Zech. 6:1, bronze mountains of opposition against YHWH's judgment on the nations
  3. Zech. 14:4-5, opposition of the nations to YHWH and the safety of God's people

Mountains often symbolize the opposition of the nations which YHWH will remove (e.g., Isa. 41:15; Jer. 13:16; 51:25).

The aspect of "two" mountains with a valley in between may foreshadow Zech. 14:4-5 (the eschatological work of the Messiah), which builds on the literal valley between the temple (Mt. Moriah) and the Mount of Olives.

If the Jerusalem area is the object of the symbol, it is also possible that the two "bronze pillars" in front of the temple itself (cf. 1 Kgs. 7:15-22) are the focus. This would imply that YHWH dwells with His people again in His rebuilt temple (cf. Dan. 9:20-27).

▣ "bronze" This was the strongest alloy known in that day (BDB 638, cf. 1 Kings 7:13-22). This description as being of bronze shows their symbolic nature.

entries.title: Zechariah Contextual Insights
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
ZECHARIAH 6

PARAGRAPH DIVISIONS OF MODERN TRANSLATIONS

NASB NKJV NRSV TEV NJB
The Four Chariots Vision of Four Chariots The Eighth Vision: Four Chariots The Vision of the Four Chariots The Eighth Vision: The Chariots
6:1-8 6:1-8 6:1-8 6:1-4 6:1-8
      6:5  
      6:6-8  
  The Command to Crown Joshua The Crowning of the Messianic Leader The Command to Crown Joshua The Votive Crown
6:9-10 6:9-13
    (12b-13)		 6:9-14 6:9-14 6:9-15a
The Symbolic Crowns        
6:11-15        
  6:14-15      
    6:15 6:15  
        6:15b

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. This eighth vision seems to parallel Zech. 1:7-17, the first vision (the same number of colored horses and the same patrolling activity in all directions; YHWH's all knowing imagery).

  2. The main thrust is God's knowledge and control of human history to accomplish His complete redemptive purposes (cf. Dan. 2:21).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  3. Zechariah 6:9-15 is not another vision, but a historical reference focused toward Joshua. This Messianic passage links the royal aspect (i.e., "crown," Zech. 6:11; "sit and rule on His throne," 6:13) and the priestly aspects ("the high priest," Zech. 6:11; "He will be a priest on His throne," 6:13).

    Yet, it must be asserted that the term "Branch" may refer to Zerubbabel (cf. Zech. 3:8). It is obvious that Joshua and Zerubbabel are linked together (cf. Zech. 4:1,14; 6:13). This linking of king and priest is also present in Ps. 110:1,4 and implied in 1 Sam. 2:35.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: The Branch of the Lord (Messianic title)

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Zechariah 6:2 "red horses"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:2 "red horses" The color red (BDB 10) is probably reddish brown when it refers to animals.

▣ "black horses" Chapters 1 and 6 of Zechariah do not parallel exactly. There are two reddish houses in chapter 1, but no black one (LXX) is specifically mentioned in the MT.

6:3
NASB  "strong dappled horses"
NKJV  "dappled horses—strong steeds"
NRSV, LXX  "dappled gray horses"
TEV  "dappled horses"
NJB  "vigorous, piebald horses"
NIV  "dappled—all of them powerful"
JPSOA  "spotted—dappled"
REB  "dappled"
Peshitta  "grizzled"

From these English translations it is obvious there are two options:

  1. the color of the horses (but different from the ones mentioned in Zech. 1:8; there seems to be no significance attached to the different colors)
  2. the strength of the horses

The Hebrew term (BDB 55; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 738) means "strength" or "might" and probably applies to all of the horses (cf. v. 7), not the color of the last horse (BDB 136, spotted or dappled, cf. Gen. 31:10,12).

entries.title: Zechariah 6:4
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:4 This parallels Zech. 1:19.

6:5
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "the four spirits of heaven"
NRSV, TEV, NJB, REB, JPSOA, LXX  "the four winds of heaven"

The Hebrew word (BDB 924) can be translated "breath," "wind," or "spirit," depending on the context. In Ezekiel 37 it is used in all three senses.

  1. breath, Ezek. 37:5,6,8,9,10 (cf. Gen. 6:17; 7:15,22)
  2. wind, Ezek. 37:9 (cf. Gen. 8:1)
  3. spirit, Ezek. 37:1,14 (cf. Gen. 1:2; 6:3; 41:38; 45:27)

The phrase, "the four winds," is also used in Jer. 49:36; Dan. 7:2; 11:4; Rev. 7:1, in a universal sense (see note at Zech 5:3; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 495-6).

This same group of angelic beings is called

  1. four winds in Zech. 2:6
  2. four messengers in Ps. 110:4

SPECIAL TOPIC: BREATH, WIND, SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE, I. D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #2

▣ "standing before" This is a Hebrew idiom (BDB 426, KB 427, Hithpael INFINITIVE), which denotes angelic service. Here it speaks of angelic beings presenting themselves before YHWH as in Job 1:6; 2:1.

▣ "the Lord" This seems to be a standardized imagery for YHWH and adon (cf. Zech. 4:14; Micah 4:13), but in v. 4, it refers to the interpreting angel.

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (aadon and kurios)

▣ "of all the earth" This interpretive question is the meaning of erets. It can denote several geographical areas. In this context, Palestine seems to be the focus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY EARTH (erets)

entries.title: Zechariah 6:6 "north"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:6 "north" The term "north" refers to the direction from which the invaders of Palestine from Mesopotamia came. Because of the desert to the east of Palestine, these empires followed the Euphrates River to the coastal plain and then went south. Therefore, "the north" became an idiom of peril, invasion, death, exile.

However, in this context, it refers to YHWH sending angelic help to His exiled people in Babylon.

▣
NASB, NKJV, LXX, Peshitta  "go forth after them"
NRSV  "go toward the west country"
TEV  "were going to the west"
NJB  "following them"
NIV  "toward the west"
REB  "to the far west"
JPSOA  "have gone out"

The Hebrew text has the term (BDB 29) "after them" (NASB, NKJV) or "following them" (NJB). This means the black and white horses would go the same direction. It is possible to understand the PREPOSITION in Zech. 6:6 as

  1. "beside," implying another direction (i.e., west)
  2. "the region of the west" (NRSV, REB, JPSOA footnote)
  3. "toward the sea" (NEB), which seems to fit the context of "four" representing the land of Palestine

The UBS Text Project, p. 405, gives "towards behind them" an "A" rating.

6:7
NASB  "the strong ones"
NKJV  "strong steeds"
NRSV  "steeds"
TEV, JPSOA  "dappled horses"
NJB  "vigorously eager"
NET  "all these strong ones"
NIV  "the powerful horses"
REB  "the roan"
JPSOA  "the dappled ones"
LXX  "the dappled gray"
Peshitta  "the red horses"

The term "strong" (BDB 55) was used in Zech. 6:3 to describe all of the four colored horses, so too here, instead of a color (NET, p. 1670, #8; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 443).

The JPSOA footnote suggests an emendation that reads this phrase as "the bay ones will go out to the region of the east."

▣
NASB, NRSV, LXX  "to go to patrol the earth"
NKJV  "to walk to and fro throughout the earth"
TEV  "to go and inspect the earth"
NJB  "to patrol the world"
NET, Peshitta  "to go and walk about over the earth"
NIV  "straining to go throughout the earth"
REB, JPSOA  "to set off and range over the whole earth"

These angels were ready and eager to serve YHWH, but they must wait for His permission (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE, "go" and BDB 229, KB 246, Hithpael IMPERATIVE, "partrol"). They are a symbolic way of representing His omniscient presence and knowledge, as does the "four colored horses" of Zech. 1:8-11.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:8 "Then He cried out to me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:8 "Then He cried out to me" The NASB has the PRONOUN capitalized, which means the translation committee thought the one speaking was YHWH because of the command, "Go," in v. 7 and "My" wrath in v. 8.

▣
NASB  "have appeased"
NKJV  "have given rest"
NRSV  "have set. . .at rest"
TEV, Peshitta  "have quieted"
NJB  "brought. . .to rest"
REB, LXX  "rest"

This Hebrew term (BDB 628, KB 679) is the Hiphil PERFECT, meaning "to cause to rest" or "give rest." It is also used several times of YHWH's wrath being appeased in Ezekiel (cf. Zech. 5:13; 16:42; 24:13). But here, in context, it seems to refer to His angels sent by Him to the north that appeased His wrath.

▣
NASB  "My wrath"
NKJV  "My Spirit"
NRSV, NJB, REB, Peshitta  "my spirit"
TEV  "the Lord's" anger
LXX  "my rage"
JPSOA  "have done my pleasure"

Literally it is "my spirit" referring to YHWH's personified wrath. This may refer to Cyrus II's defeat (cf. Isa. 44:28-54:1) of Babylon. YHWH is in control of history (cf. Dan. 2:21).

The JPSOA translation is a suggested emendation based on post-biblical usage of the MT words.

Zechariah 6:7 and 8 are direct speech, but from whom? It is difficult in this type of literature to identify the speakers. Sometimes the prophet (cf. Zech. 6:9-12) and the angels speak for God (cf.Zech. 6:7). However, this is complicated in Messianic texts when the Messiah (angel of the Lord, cf. Zech. 3:6-8) speaks as God. I think it best to understand Zech. 6:7 and 8 as YHWH speaking and 6:5-6 as the angel speaking.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ANGEL OF THE LORD

entries.title: Zechariah 6:9 "The word of the Lord also came to me"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:9 "The word of the Lord also came to me" This is a prophetic formula which introduces a new revelation from YHWH (cf. Zech. 1:1,7; 4:6,8; 6:9; 7:1,4,8; 8:1,18). Theologically this asserts that the information is not from human origin, but from a divine source. Inspiration is a crucial, non-compromisable truth (i.e., 2 Tim. 3:16; 2 Pet. 1:20-21). The Bible is not just another "holy" book of the world religions! Inspiration is difficult to define, but it must include editors and compilers.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRUSTWORTHINESS OF THE BIBLE

6:10
NASB  "take an offering from the exiles"
NKJV  "receive the gift from the captives"
NRSV, NJB  "collect. . .from the exiles"
TEV, REB  "take the gifts given by the exiles"
NET  "choose some people from among the exiles"
JPSOA  "Receive from the exiled community"
LXX  "take the things from the captivity"
Peshitta  "take of them of the captivity"

Most English translations understand the VERB (BDB 542, KB 534, Qal INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE) as referring to

  1. the silver and gold given by the exiles in Persia
  2. but the RSV, NAB, and NET Bibles assume it refers to a select group from among the exiles as a way to honor all those Jews who chose to return

There is no stated OBJECT of the VERB in the Hebrew text.

I think this refers to the returning Jewish Levites and priests from Babylon coming with a gift from the Persian court to help rebuild the temple (cf. Ezra 7:13-16; 8:24-30). They are told to go immediately to Josiah's house (another priest, cf. Jer. 29:25,29), who was possibly their host.

▣ "enter the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, where they have arrived from Babylon" It is possible to interpret this as

  1. all four men named had just come from Persia with gifts for the new temple. Josiah's lineage is given because he was the most prominent of the group (cf. Joyce Baldwin, Tyndale Old Testament Commentaries, "Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi," p. 132).
  2. Another way is to see Josiah as a resident of Jerusalem, where the group of three men stayed (cf. H.C. Leupold, Exposition of Zechariah, p. 121).
  3. If so, the concluding phrase is out of normal order (cf. UBS' Handbook on Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, pp. 170-171).

entries.title: Zechariah 6:11 "crown"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:11 "crown" This is PLURAL (used with a SINGULAR VERB in Zech. 6:14), but it seems to refer to one crown, possibly a double crown (like those from Egypt) symbolizing "the two offices" (cf. Zech. 6:13). The Hebrew term (BDB 742) does not refer to a priestly crown (BDB 63, cf. Exod 29:6; Lev. 8:9), but to

  1. a royal one (cf. Zech. 9:16; 1 Chr. 20:2; Isa. 28:5; 2:3; Jer. 13:18; Ezek. 21:26)
  2. a way to honor someone, but not necessarily royalty

▣ "on the head of Joshua. . .the high priest" Some theories relating to the high priest crowned as king are:

  1. for political reasons Zerubbabel could not be crowned (see F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, p. 37)
  2. a textual error
  3. a scribal change
  4. Joshua was a type of Christ as both priest and king as Jesus was in the NT in the book of Hebrews (cf. Heb. 5:1-10; 7:1-25; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MELCHIZEDEK)
  5. the high priest, after Zerubbabel's death, took over the office of king (as did eight Hasmonian rulers)

entries.title: Zechariah 6:12 "Then say to him, 'Thus says the Lord of hosts'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:12 "Then say to him, 'Thus says the Lord of hosts'" What a powerful affirmation of YHWH's desire to communicate (cf. Hag. 1:2,5,7; 2:6; Zech. 1:14; 6:12; 8:2,20). YHWH is giving specific information through His chosen speaker (i.e., a prophet). The exact method of inspiration is not always known, but here it is a verbal message (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION and SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION).

It is difficult to follow the levels of direct and indirect speech in Zechariah. Here it is obvious the Lord directs Zechariah to speak on His behalf. Sometimes the angel of the Lord speaks on YHWH's behalf. It is possible that in certain contexts the angel of the Lord is the Messiah. The ANTECEDENT to the PRONOUNS is not always evident from the context.

SPECIAL TOPIC: The Angel of the Lord

▣ "a man" The Messiah will be a human person (cf. Dan. 7:13). In Zechariah angels are designated as men (e.g., Zech. 1:8,10; 2:1,4), as well as the Messiah (symbolized by Joshua and Zerubbabel). YHWH will use human instrumentality to reveal Himself, accomplish redemption, and provide an example for all other human beings (i.e., Exod. 3:7-9 and vv. 10-12).

▣ "Branch" This word (BDB 855; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 148-9) means "sprout" in Isa. 4:2; 11:1; 53:2; Jer. 23:5; 33:15. It is a title for the Messiah.

In Zechariah (cf. Zech. 3:8; 6:12) it refers to Zerubbabel as a type of the Messiah (cf. Ibn Ezra and Rashi). The name, Zerubbabel, in Akkadian, means "shoot of Babylon." This was possibly a play on his name since he rebuilt the temple in 516 B.C., but it is really an ultimate reference to Jesus. Zerubbabel is an ancestor of Jesus in Matt. 1:12-13; Luke 3:27.

This title and the matching VERB ("will branch out," Qal IMPERFECT) appear together in this verse.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BRANCH (MESSIANIC TITLE)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JESUS THE NAZARENE

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣
NASB, NKJV, NRSV, NIV, REB, JPSOA  "for He will branch out"
TEV  "will flourish"
NJB  "there will be a branching out"
NET  "who will sprout up"
LXX  "he shall sprout"
Peshitta  "rise"

The title "Branch" is used as a VERB (BDB 855, KB 1033, Qal IMPERFECT). This may imply

  1. a worldwide kingdom (cf. Isa. 45:22; 52:10; Micah 5:4; Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:47; Acts 1:8)
  2. a renewed (Davidic) kingdom (cf. 2 Samuel 7; Isa. 11:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TENSION BETWEEN OLD COVENANT PROPHETIC MODELS AND NEW COVENANT APOSTOLIC MODELS

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "He will build the temple" This seems to refer to Zerubbabel historically (cf. Zech. 4:9), but to Jesus eschatologically. The temple that Jesus will build seems to be spiritual (cf. John 2:19-21), although some see it as the temple of Ezekiel 38-40. The book of the Revelation speaks of a heavenly temple (cf. Rev. 3:12; 7:15; 11:1-2,19; 14:15,17; 15:5,6,8; 16:1,17). However, when New Jerusalem comes down out of heaven (cf. Rev. 21:22), there is no temple mentioned. The book of Hebrews speaks of a heavenly tabernacle into which Jesus entered as High Priest to once and for all offer Himself as a sacrifice to God on our behalf (cf. Hebrews 8-10), but it is not mentioned anywhere else in Scripture, although the detailed plans of Exodus 25-27 seem to imply a heavenly original pattern.

The term "house" (BDB 108) is used often (cf. Zech. 1:16; 3:7; 4:9; 8:9) to refer to the temple (BDB 228). However, in Zech. 8:9 both terms are used synonymously, so there is no intended distinction.

entries.title: Zechariah 6:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:13 This seems

  1. to combine in one person both kingly and priestly offices (cf. Ps. 104:1,4)
  2. to be an emphasis on two offices (i.e., two thrones). This would attribute to Zerubbabel the rebuilding of the temple, and to Joshua, administrating in it.
  3. The LXX has "and the priest shall be on his right." Two leaders, one thrown.

▣ "the counsel of peace" These two leaders would reign together in perfect cooperation and harmony. The peace (shalom, BDB 102) between them would bless the nation they serve and reflect the God of the nation they represent.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom)

entries.title: Zechariah 6:14
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:14 These four Hebrew names refer to those mentioned in Zech. 6:10, but two of the names are different. The Peshitta, NRSV, TEV, and NIV take the word hen (BDB 336), which means "grace," "favor," or "kindness" ("gracious one," possibly their host) as referring to Josiah, son of Zephaniah (cf. Zech. 6:10, JPSOA footnote).

The UBS Text Project, vol. 5, p. 467, suggests that the person "Helem" is the same as "Heldai" in v. 10.

  1. v. 10 was a nick-name
  2. v. 14 is an official title
  3. the LXX has "Heldai" in both places

The Hebrew language often uses different spellings for the same person. For example, there are four ways to spell Joshua.

  1. Yehoshu'a, Deut. 3:21
  2. Hoshe'a, Deut. 32:44
  3. Yeshoshu'a, Joshua 1:1
  4. Yeshu'a, Neh. 8:17

The same person can also go by several names (nick names, titles). For example, Moses' father-in-law:

  1. Jethro, Exod. 3:1
  2. Jether, Exod. 4:18
  3. Reuel, Exod. 2:18
  4. Priest of Median, Exod. 3:1
  5. Hobab, Jdgs. 4:11
▣
NASB  "the crown will become a reminder in the temple of the Lord"
NKJV  "the elaborate crown shall be for a memorial in the temple
  of the Lord"
NRSV  "the crown shall be in the care of. . .as a memorial in the temple
  of the Lord"
TEV  "the crown will be a memorial in the Lord's temple in honor of"
NJB  "the crown will serve. . .as a memorial of favor in Yahweh's
  sanctuary"
NIV  "the crown will be given to...as a memorial in the temple of
  the Lord"
JPSOA  "the crown shall remain in the temple of the Lord as a
  memorial to"

This majestic coronation of Joshua as symbolic co-ruler with the Branch is a powerful symbol of the coming Priest-King Messiah (cf. Psalm 110)! Exactly how this is related to the men listed is uncertain. This event is far more significant than just a memorial to four men. This is the focus of the preceding visions. It had national and international implications (cf. Zech. 6:15).

The crown (BDB 742 I, PLURAL) was obviously not worn everyday, but displayed as a fulfilled and to-be fulfilled promise of restoration and complete eschatological restoration!

entries.title: Zechariah 6:15 "Those who are far off"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
6:15 "Those who are far off" Historically this refers to

  1. the Jews of the Diaspora (cf. in the Fertile Crescent and Egypt)
  2. the Persian court, possibly represented by the three men of Zech. 6:10 and 14
  3. eschatologically it refers to the Gentiles (cf. Zech. 2:11; 8:20-23; Isa. 2:2-4; 56:6-8; 60:5c-9,10; Micah 4:1-5; Eph. 2:11-22)

▣ "Then you will know that the Lord of Hosts has sent me" If this is historical, then this is referring to Zechariah (cf. Zech. 2:8,9,11; 4:9). If it is eschatological then it refers to Jesus. The inclusion of Gentiles into God's covenant plan does not fit the historical setting of the post-exilic period (esp. Nehemiah and Haggai). The PRONOUNS are ambiguous in this book and could refer to

  1. YHWH
  2. the prophet
  3. an angel in the visions
  4. the Messiah

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "it will take place if you completely obey the Lord your God" Notice that there is a conditional element in these promises (cf. Zech. 3:7). This is a quote from Deut. 28:1 (Deuteronomy 27-29 contains the Covenant Cursing and Blessing Litany; also see Leviticus 26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. What are the eight visions trying to convey to us?
  2. Do the visions relate to the post-exilic period or to the end-time?
  3. Why is Joshua crowned in Zech. 6:11 and not Zerubbabel?
  4. Will Jesus rebuild the Jewish temple?

 

Copyright © 2014 Bible Lessons International

entries.title: Zechariah 7:1 "fourth year of King Darius"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:1 "fourth year of King Darius" This is almost two years later than the initial eight visions (cf. Zech. 1:1,7). The dating of this chapter is very specific.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF PERSIA

▣ "the word of the Lord came to Zechariah" This phrase introduces a new revelation. It also seems to mark the paragraph divisions of this chapter. Zechariah did not choose the time or subject. This is YHWH's message (cf. Zech. 7:4).

The Hebrew word dbr (BDB 182) is used regularly for God's revelation (cf. Zech. 1:1,6,7; 4:6; 7:1,4,7,12; 8:1,18; 9:1; 11:11; 12:1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

▣ "the fourth day of the ninth month" This would possibly be December 7, 518 B.C. (cf. UBS, A Handbook on Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, p. 180).

▣ "Chislev" This is a month in the Babylonian calendar (cf. Neh. 1:1), approximately November or December.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANE CALENDARS

7:2
NASB  "the town of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regemmelech"
NKJV, NRSV  "the people sent Sherezer with Regem-Melech"
TEV  "the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and
  Regemmelech"
NJB  "Bethel sent Sharezer"
JPSOA  "Bethel-sharezer and Regem-melech. . .sent"
Peshitta  "sent to Bethel Sherezar and Rab-mag, and the
  king. . .had sent word to pray for him"
REB  "Bether-sharezer sent Regem-melech"

The Hebrew is very ambiguous. There are several theories:

  1. King James translates "Bethel" as "the house of God," not a town
  2. RSV, TEV, NIV and JB have "Bethel," which is a cultic city about twelve miles north of Jerusalem and the center of calf worship in Israel during 922-722 B.C.
  3. NEB combines "Bethel" and "Sharezer" into one name. Similar compounds using Sharezer are found in Jer. 39:3, while compound names using Bethel are found in Babylonian documents and in the Elephantine Papyri (cf. W. F. Albright, Archaeology and the Religion of Israel, p. 169)
  4. the term "Regemmelech" (BDB 920) means "the king's spokesman" in Ugaritic (the Syriac translation has "Rab-mag," which was an official title, cf. Jer. 39:3,13), which implies that Darius or influential Jews sent two men (JPSOA, Bethel-Sharezer and Regem-Melech).
▣
NASB  "to seek the favor"
NKJV, Peshitta  "to pray before"
NRSV, NJB, REB, JPSOA  "to entreat the favor"
TEV  "to pray for"
LXX  "to appease"

This is the INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT of the Piel stem (BDB 318 II, KB 316), which denotes the cessation of hostility (cf. Dan. 9:13), as well as the presence of YHWH's blessing and acceptance (cf. Ps. 119:59). This same VERB is used in Zech. 8:21-22 for what the nations will seek from Him.

Just a brief theological note about the meaning of this Hebrew VERB in the Piel stem.

  1. C. H. Dodd, The Bible and the Greeks has asserted that this VERB stem implies "expiation" not "propitiation."
  2. This has been refuted by George Eldon Ladd, Theology of the New Testament (which I highly recommend).
  3. Ladd's position is also affirmed by Leon Morris (see Millard Erickson, Christian Theology, 2nd ed., p. 828).
  4. both BDB and KB assert that in the Piel stem it denotes "appeasement" in Zech. 7:2; 8:21; Mal. 1:9

SPECIAL TOPIC: BASIC PROCEDURES FOR A BIBLICAL WORD STUDY

entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
ZECHARIAH 7

PARAGRAPH DIVISIONS OF MODERN TRANSLATIONS

      7:2-3 A Survey of the Nation's Past
  7:4-7   7:4-7 7:4-14
  Disobedience Resulted in Exile   Disobedience, the Cause of Exile

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. Zechariah, chapters 7-8 form a literary unit. The theological issue is the Jews' covenant faithfulness (cf. Zech. 7:9-13) vs. religious ritual (i.e. national fasting, cf. Zech. 7:3; 8:19).

  2. YHWH used the Jews' disobedience and subsequent dispersion for His own redemptive purposes (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36; Romans 9-11). God will restore faithful Jews and welcome believing nations to Himself (cf. Zech. 8:20-23).
    SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

  3. The promised covenant renewal still requires obedience (cf. Zech. 6:15 and 8:16-17). The covenant requirements of the Old Covenant and the New Covenant are the same.
    1. repentance
    2. faith
    3. obedience
    4. perseverance

      The Old Covenant was based on human performance, but the New Covenant is based on a new heart, a new mind, and a new spirit from God (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). However, both seek a godly people to reveal YHWH's character to the nations whom He loves and desires that they know Him!
      SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT
      SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP
      SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

  4. For a good discussion of fasting see
    1. New International Dictionary of Old Testament Theology and Exegesis, vol. 3, pp. 780-783
    2. SPECIAL TOPIC: FASTING

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Zechariah 7:3 "speaking to the priests. . .the prophets"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:3 "speaking to the priests. . .the prophets" The priests would refer to those who had returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel and Joshua or Ezra. It is uncertain to whom "the prophets" refers. Haggai and Zechariah are the only ones known by name. I think both Joel and Obadiah were also early post-exilic prophets. Whomever they were these emissaries came to the representatives of YHWH asking about the continuance of a fast denoting the destruction of Jerusalem, now that the Jews had returned to Jerusalem.

▣ "Shall I weep in the fifth month" This refers to a national day of mourning (fasting) which the Jews initiated to remember the fall of Jerusalem and the destruction of the temple (cf. 2 Kings 25). But now that they were back in Judah and the temple was rebuilt, should they continue this annual fast?

▣
NASB  "abstain"
NKJV, REB  "fast"
NRSV, JPSOA  "practice abstinence"
TEV, NJB  "fasting"
Peshitta  "separating myself"
LXX  "the holy offering"

The term (BDB 634) in the Niphal means to "dedicate oneself to God," "treat with awe," or "fast." In this context "fast" is best. Context determines meaning!

▣ "as I have done these many years" This again is an allusion to the 70 year prophecy of exile by Jeremiah (cf. Jer. 25:8-11; 29:10; Dan. 9:2,24; Zech. 7:5).

entries.title: Zechariah 7:5 "Say to all the people of the land"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:5 "Say to all the people of the land" This is an idiom for the common, non-leadership (cf. Jer. 34:10; Hag. 2:4) people of God's covenant promise (i.e., Jews). For a good discussion of the way this idiom developed and changed through Israel's history see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel: Social Institutions, vol. 1, pp. 70-72.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PEOPLE OF THE LAND

▣ "seventh month" This refers to another national fast day to remember the death of Gedaliah, the Babylonian appointed Jewish governor (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:25; Jer. 40:1-41:3). I think that possibly the ambiguous terms in Zech. 7:2 and the fast days commended (cf. Zech. 8:19) related to a delegation of Jews from Babylon to Jerusalem to discuss the status of the official ritual calendar.

▣ "seventy years" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SEVENTY YEARS

▣ "was it actually for Me that you fasted" YHWH did not initiate these fasts and really they were done out of self pity more than worship (cf. Isa. 1:11-12; 58:1-12). YHWH is the One who sent Assyria (Isa. 10:5) and Babylon (Jer. 13:9).

entries.title: Zechariah 7:6 "When you eat and drink"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:6 "When you eat and drink" This is sarcasm. They were fasting and/or feasting for themselves, not for YHWH (cf. Isa. 29:13; Col. 2:20-33).

entries.title: Zechariah 7:7 "the former prophets"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:7 "the former prophets" See note at Zech. 1:4.

▣ "when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous" This refers to the time before the Babylonian exile. Nebuchadnezzar II conducted four deportations.

  1. 605 B.C. ‒ Daniel and his three friends
  2. 597 B.C. ‒ Ezekiel and 10,000 skilled Jews
  3. 586 B.C. ‒ Jerusalem and the temple destroyed and most of the remaining population exiled
  4. 582 B.C. ‒ after the murder of Gedaliah the Babylonian military returned and exiled everyone they could find

▣ "the Negev" This (BDB 616) refers to the uninhabited pasture land in southern Judea.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GEOGRAPHICAL DIVISIONS OF THE PROMISED LAND

▣ "the foothills" This is literally "shephelah" (BDB 1050), which refers to the coastal plain along the Mediterranean.

At the time of Haggai and Zechariah neither of these geographical areas belonged to the returned Jews under Cyrus II's edict. Zerubbabel only controlled a small area around the city of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Zechariah 7:8
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 7:8 Is this a textual marker to designate a new context? Joyce Baldwin, in Tyndale Old Testament Commentaries, "Haggai, Zecharian, Malachi," (p. 145), says it is an editorial addition that misunderstood the unity of the passage.

entries.title: Zechariah 7:9-10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:9-10 The prophets always direct the people back to their covenant responsibilities. They are "covenant watch dogs"! Zechariah 7:9-10 go back to the Mosaic covenant and its social requirements.

As an example, the Ten Commandants have requirements towards God (which they had violated, cf. Zech. 7:9-10). The blessings of God as well as the cursings of God are related to covenant fidelity (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 27-29). These requirements and guidelines for life were not new or surprising to these returning Jews.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

entries.title: Zechariah 7:9 "Dispense true justice"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:9 "Dispense true justice" There is a word play between the NOUN CONSTRUCT (BDB 1048) and the Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 1047, KB 1622). Covenant people are to treat each other fairly (cf. Micah 6:8). This particular phrase refers to judicial discussions (e.g., Lev. 19:15; Deut. 1:16-17; Prov. 31:9; Ezek. 18:8; 45:9), but has a wider implication of appropriate covenant relationships between all the members of God's people. This very term is repeated in Zech. 8:16. Injustice offends God (cf. Hosea 4:1-6).

▣ "kindness" This word is hesed (BDB 338), the special covenant NOUN which speaks of YHWH's longsuffering covenant loyalty (possibly best understood as family love). YHWH is a faithful, loving God and He demands the same of His people. For a good discussion see New International Dictionary of Old Testament Theology and Exegesis, vol. 2, pp. 211-218 and Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 111-116.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "compassion" The term (BDB 933) originally had a family orientation ("from the womb"). This same term was used earlier in the angel's prayer to YHWH about not having "compassion" for Jerusalem. The two terms, "kindness" and "compassion" are used in Dan. 1:9 to describe YHWH's graciousness to Daniel through Nebuchadnezzar's overseer. As He treats us, we as His people should treat one another (cf. Phil. 2:5ff; 1 John 3:16). Our attitudes and actions show to whom we belong!

entries.title: Zechariah 7:10 "do not oppress the widow. . .the orphan. . .the stranger. . .the poor"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:10 "do not oppress the widow. . .the orphan. . .the stranger. . .the poor" The NEGATED VERB (BDB 798, KB 897) is a Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense. Justice without partiality is a recurrent theme of the book of Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 1:17; 10:17; 16:19; 24:14,17). YHWH defends the defenseless.

For an expanded discussion on YHWH's care for

  1. widows, see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 413-415
  2. orphans, see NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 570-571
▣
NASB, JPSOA  "the stranger"
NKJV, NRSV  "the alien"
NJB  "the foreigner"
Peshitta  "the proselyte"
REB  "resident alien"
LXX  "the guest"

This is the Hebrew term (BDB 158) which denotes a resident alien. These were free people, not slaves, but they had limited civil rights. YHWH was seen as their protector and defender as He was for all socially deprived, powerless, and poor people (cf. Exod. 22:21-24; Deut. 10:18). A special third year tithe was received locally to aid society's needy (cf. Deut. 14:28-29; see SPECIAL TOPIC: TITHING).

For a good discussion of Israelite social order see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel: Social Institutions, vol. 1, pp. 69-79.

▣ "do not devise evil in your hearts" This VERB (BDB 362, KB 359) is another Qal IMPERFECT used as a JUSSIVE. This refers to legal procedures (cf. Zech. 8:17) with an emphasis on proper attitude and motives. Treat others with respect as fellow covenant partners. Evil is always self-centered; love is always others-centered!

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEART

entries.title: Zechariah 7:11-12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:11-12 This is a series of four parallel phrases describing the attitudes of disrespect and disobedience of YHWH's people.

  1. "they refused to pay attention"
  2. "they turned a stubborn shoulder" (cf. Neh. 9:29)
  3. "they stopped their ears from hearing" (cf. Jer. 5:21; 6:10; Ezek. 12:2)
  4. "they made their hearts like flint so that they could not hear"
  5. also note Ezek. 7:13a and compare Isa. 6:9-10

entries.title: Zechariah 7:12 "They made their hearts like flint"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:12 "They made their hearts like flint" This Hebrew term (BDB 1038 I; NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 167) refers to some kind of very hard material like corundum or diamond (cf. Jer. 17:1). It is used as imagery here of the hardness of the Jewish ancestors' hearts toward their God. This same image of hardness is used in a positive way in Ezek. 3:9 for YHWH equipping the prophet to face strong opposition.

This is active refusal to listen and heed YHWH's word and will (the opposite of shema). His people were in open, active, willful rebellion!

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

▣ "sent His Spirit through the former prophets" This refers to the inspiration of the OT prophets (cf. Zech. 1:4; 7:7; Neh. 9:20,30) by the agency of the Holy Spirit (cf. 1 Pet. 1:11; 2I Pet. 1:21; "the God breathed" of 2 Tim. 3:16).

Often in the OT the Spirit is a way of referring to God (e.g., Ps. 139:7-8; Isa. 40:13; 60:10-11) or God's creative activity (e.g., Gen. 1:2). God energizes humans to perform tasks with His strength and wisdom (e.g., Exod. 28:3; 31:3; 35:31,34; Jdgs. 3:10; 6:34; 11:29; 13:54; 14:6,19; 15:14).

The OT does not clearly reveal the NT concept of three divine persons with one eternal essence, but it does begin to reveal a personal plurality in Deity. The problem is that plurality and monotheism are hard to reconcile. The church is forced to articulate a triune unity because of the NT affirmations of:

  1. the Deity of Jesus
  2. the personality of the Spirit

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

▣ "therefore great wrath came from the Lord of hosts" This willful disrespect and disobedience caused the curses of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28 to become a reality (cf. Dan. 9:1-19).

This disobedience with its resulting wrath (cf. Zech. 7:14) caused the nations to misunderstand YHWH and His redemptive purposes (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

entries.title: Zechariah 7:13 "He called"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:13 "He called" YHWH called to them through the covenants, the Exodus, the temple, and the prophets (cf. Hosea 11:2), but they would not obey!

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

▣ "they called and I would not listen" Now the tables are turned! YHWH called and they would not hear, now they call for His help, but He will not hear (cf. Isa. 1:15), not only because of their covenant disobedience, but also their covenant hypocrisy (cf. Isa. 1:11-15). If they would truly repent, YHWH would respond (cf. Isa. 1:16-20).

entries.title: Zechariah 7:14 "I scattered"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
7:14 "I scattered" YHWH is in control of history! This refers to the Babylonian Exile.

This VERB (BDB 704, KB 762) is a Piel IMPERFECT. In the ancient world a military defeat meant the defeat of the national god. Israel and Judah's defeat was not because of YHWH's weakness, but their sin (cf. Daniel 9). It was YHWH who caused both the Assyrian (cf. Isa. 10:5) and Babylonian exiles (cf. Jer. 13:9; 51:20-24).

▣ "the land is desolated" The covenant promises were rescinded (cf. Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29). The Covenant has always been conditional on God's grace and an appropriate human response.

God brought desolation (cf. Jer. 4:6) so that He could bring restoration to a repentant people. Judgment is an act of love (cf. Heb. 12:5-13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

▣
NASB  "no one went back and forth"
NKJV, LXX  "no one passed through or returned"
NRSV  "no one went to and fro"
TEV  "no one living in it"
NJB, REB, JPSOA  "no one came or went"
Peshitta  "without any one to pass through"

This unusual phrase is found only in Zech. 7:14 and 9:8. Zechariah is divided into two literary units (chapters 1-8 and 9-14). This unusual phrase appears in both units and, thereby becomes evidence for the unity of the book by one author.

entries.content: 8:1 This is a literary marker introducing a new stage of the discussion. See note at Zech. 7:1.

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. As I read and research this chapter, it again reminds me of the pain I feel for
    1. people who know God only through the Mosaic Covenant (i.e., national Israel)
    2. people who violate the Mosaic Covenant with terrible consequences (most of Israel's history, Lev. 26; Deut. 28)
    3. the Gentile nations who remained in ignorance of God for so long

  2. This chapter is a powerful promise of restoration. It uses utopian language of a future day of a secure and just society which includes all peoples.

  3. However, that society is centered by a faithful, repentant Israel with Jerusalem as its capital. This does not describe
    1. the post-exilic Judah
    2. the modern secular state of Israel
      For a good discussion of the place of modern Israel in God's plan, see the YouTube video by Steve Gregg, "The Modern State of Israel." I think it will make you rethink much that you have been told and assume to be true about Israel.

  4. Neither Jesus, nor His Apostles, ever asserts or affirms any OT promises to national Israel. Only believing Israel (i.e., Rom. 2:28-29; 9-11) is included in NT promises and salvation.

  5. My love for the Bible and my trust in God's character cause me great confusion (cf. Isa. 55:6-13). Is the NT about Israel?

  6. As a follower of Christ I must assert and cling to the priority of the New Covenant. Jesus, not Israel (i.e., Matt. 5:17-19), is the ultimate revelation of God (i.e., Matt. 5:21-48). The NT is about Jesus, not Israel!

  7. Jesus, Himself, said such harsh things to the Jews of His day (i.e., Matt. 12:34; 23:2-39; Luke 20:9-19). I have come to believe the Olivet Discourse and the book of Revelation are about God's judgment on "those who pierced Him" (cf. Rev. 1:7). For some good books on Preterism, see
    1. John Bray, Matthew 24 Fulfilled
    2. Kenneth Gentry
      1. Before Jerusalem Fell
      2. The Beast of Revelation
      3. The Apocalypse of John: A Preterist Commentary of the Book of Revelation
    3. Four Views on the Book of Revelation, several authors, note pp. 39-92
    4. Steve Gregg
      1. Revelation: Four views, Revised and Expanded
      2. Why Not Full-Preterism? A Partial-Preterist Response to a Novel Theological Innovation
      3. Many thought provoking YouTube videos on biblical issues and controversies; his website is www.thenarrowpath.com; I highly recommend this brother's Bible study and lectures on contemporary controversies.
    5. Gary DeMar
      1. Last Days Madness: Obsession of the Modern Church
      2. End Time Fiction" A Biblical Consideration of Left Behind Theology
    6. Bruce Gore, YouTube video, "The Apocalypse in Space and Time" (10 lectures with detailed historical and Early Church Father quotes; very detailed and interesting)

  8. So, I affirm that the Old Covenant has been fulfilled (Matt. 5:17-19). It is still inspired and relevant, but it has been superseded (cf. Acts 15; Galatians 3; the book of Hebrews).

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Zechariah 8:2 "the Lord of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:2 "the Lord of hosts" This was a common post-exilic title.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "I am exceedingly jealous" See full notes at Zech. 1:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEALOUSY/ZEAL

▣ "Zion" This is one of the seven hills of Jerusalem, but it came to stand for the entire city, including Mount Moriah on which the temple stood. See note at Zech. 1:14.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

▣
NASB, NRSV  "with great wrath"
NKJV  "with great fervor"
TEV  "made me angry"
NJB  "furious jealousy"
REB, JPSOA  "fiercely jealous"
LXX  "with great jealousy"
Peshitta  "with great zeal"

The Hebrew root (BDB 404) means "to be hot." The implication here is YHWH's passion (the Piel stem means "to conceive"). This term is often used by the seventh century prophets (i.e., Jeremiah and Ezekiel, note specifically Ezek. 36:6-7). The interpretive question is how to understand "wrath." Is it meant to refer

  1. to YHWH's hot passion for His people?
  2. to His anger at those nations He chose to discipline His people?

I believe the Hebrew phrase, "I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, with great wrath, I am jealous" best fits option #2 (cf. NIV, REB). This is not the same Hebrew word as Zech. 7:12 (BDB 893).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

entries.title: Zechariah 8:3 "I will return to Zion"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:3 "I will return to Zion" YHWH had left the temple in Jerusalem (cf. Ezekiel 10) because of the Jews' idolatry (cf. Ezekiel 8), before the city was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar II (cf. Ezekiel 9). YHWH Himself went to be with the Jews in exile (cf. Ezekiel 1). The faithful ones in exile would be the new people of God.

His return (BDB 996, KB 1427; Qal PERFECT) was the confirmation that He had forgiven His people and renewed His covenant with them.

▣ "will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem" There is no greater blessing than the personal presence of YHWH with His people (e.g., Exod. 25:8; Lev. 26:11-12; Num. 5:3; 35:23; Deut. 23:14; Isa. 7:14, "Immanuel"). The sacrificial system and temple were the hope of sinful people who YHWH would forgive (cf. Exod. 29:45).

Notice these two phrases are parallel with (both Qal PERFECTS) each other, as are the next two phrases in Zech. 8:3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

▣
NASB, NKJV, Peshitta  "the City of Truth"
NRSV, TEV  "the faithful city"
NJB  "the Faithful City"
REB, JPSOA  "the City of Faithfulness"
LXX  "a city that is true"

This could also be translated "city of faithfulness." The faithful God had returned to the faithless descendants of Abraham.

In Isa. 1:21-23 Jerusalem is sarcastically called "the faithful city," yet in Isa. 1:24-26 YHWH the Faithful will change her and forgive her so that she would truly be "the faithful city" (cf. Zech. 8:2b) again.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO CITIES IN ISAIAH

▣ "the mountain of the Lord" This refers to the temple area or Mt. Moriah ("YHWH provides"). This is the place where:

  1. Melchizedek was anointed priest/king, Genesis 14
  2. Abraham was to offer Isaac, Genesis 22
  3. David offered a sacrifice to stop God's judgment, 1 Chr. 21:9-30
  4. Solomon built the temple, 2 Chr. 3:1

SPECIAL TOPIC: MORIAH

▣ "the Holy Mountain" It is holy because YHWH's presence is there. His presence must be reflected in His people (cf. Deut. 28:9). They must be different; they must be like Him (e.g., Lev. 19:2 [1 Pet. 1:16]; Matt. 5:48). For a good discussion of "holy," see Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT.

See a good note on the biblical use of "mountain" in NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 1051-1054.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY

entries.title: Zechariah 8:4 "old men and old women"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:4 "old men and old women" Most of the elderly died because of the exile and those who grew old in Babylon could not easily return, therefore, elderly people in the land was a sign of lengthy prosperity (cf. Deut. 28:3) or the New Age (cf. Isa. 65:20).

entries.title: Zechariah 8:5 "boys and girls playing"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:5 "boys and girls playing" This was a sign of God's blessing (cf. Deut. 28:4) and normal social life. This shows the reversal of YHWH's curses (i.e., the fall of Jerusalem, cf. Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29) and His restored presence and blessing (i.e., Isa. 65:17-23; Jer. 31:12-13)!

entries.title: Zechariah 8:6 "If it is too difficult"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:6 "If it is too difficult" The Jewish people had become accustomed to captivity and judgment so these promises overwhelmed them! The term "difficult" (BDB 810, Niphal IMPERFECT) also means "wonderful." See note at Dan. 8:24.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS

▣ "the remnant of this people" The Hebrew term "remnant" (BDB 984) basically means "the remainder," "what is left," "the residue." In the prophets it takes on a special meaning, "the faithful remnant," which refers to the few descendants of Abraham who believed, trusted, and worshiped YHWH. It is these He would restore (cf. Isa. 37:4,32; 46:3; Jer. 23:3; 31:7; Micah 2:12; 5:7,8; 7:18; Zeph. 2:7,9; Ezra 9:14; Zech. 8:6,11,12). The difficulty about this term is the time factor. Does it refer to

  1. the post-exilic period (see SPECIAL TOPIC: POST EXILIC CHART)
  2. the end-time (notice the phrase in Zech. 8:6, "in those days")

This may be an example of multiple fulfillment prophecy.

SEE SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

▣ "will it also be too difficult in My sight" There is a faith connection between YHWH's acts and the faith of His people. However, even if YHWH's people do not have faith, He still acts. He is committed to sinful humanity's redemption (cf. Zech. 8:7-8; Ezek. 36:22-38).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

entries.title: Zechariah 8:7 "save"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:7 "save" The Hebrew VERB "save" (BDB 446, KB 448 Hiphil PARTICIPLE, see SPECIAL TOPIC: SALVATION (OT Term) is used in several senses.

  1. Hiphil = "to deliver" (cf. Zech. 9:9; Jer. 30:7-11; 31:7-8) or "to give victory" (e.g., Isa. 59:16; 63:5)
  2. Niphal = "to be liberated," "to be saved," or "to be victorious"

It is used of the activity of YHWH on behalf of His people (cf. Zech. 8:7,13; 9:16; 10:6; 12:7). He delivers those who trust Him (e.g., Zech. 8:6; Ps. 37:40; 86:2).

Just a note to acknowledge that modern scholarship is still uncertain about the origin or root meaning of this term. It has been assumed that it is from an Arabic root meaning "to be wide or spacious," but there is not a consensus.

In this context YHWH is promising to deliver His people from exile and restore them to the Promised Land. However, the apocalyptic nature of the book projects this promise into the future as well as the present. It surely refers to the return to Jerusalem in 538 B.C. (Cyrus' decree), but since "the nations" (e.g., Zech. 2:11; 8:20-23) are included and the concept of Messiah is revealed and expanded in chapters 9-14, then this must also have an eschatological focus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "east. . .west" These compass directions are used in the universal sense as in Ps. 50:1; 113:3; Isa. 59:19; Mal. 1:11.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:8 "My people and I will be their God"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:8 "My people and I will be their God" This is covenant language (e.g., Lev. 26:12; Deut. 4:20; 18:2; 29:12-13; Jer. 31:33; 32:38; Hosea 2:23) and clearly shows that the covenant is restored.

"God" is Elohim; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

▣ "truth" This Hebrew word (BDB 54) means "firmness," "faithfulness," or "truth." Originally it referred to a stable stance and then came to be used as imagery for that which is trustworthy, faithful or reliable. This then becomes a description of YHWH (e.g., Ps. 71:22; 117:2; 146:6; Isa. 38:18-19; Neh. 9:33). Faithless, fallen humanity's only hope is in the unchanging, faithful mercy of God!

This term is used in Zechariah 8 several times (cf. Zech. 8:3,8,16 [twice], 19) in the sense of "truth." In Zech. 7:9 and 8:16 it refers to a true or faithful testimony in court. Zechairah 8:16 and 19 are parallel and speak of the truthful and trustworthy relationship between covenant partners in society. Truth has a corporate societal focus. Truth is relational as well as propositional!

For a good discussion of this Hebrew word in all its forms see New International Dictionary of Old Testament Theology and Exegesis, vol. 1, pp. 427-433.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

SPECIAL TOPIC: TRUTH/TRUE

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "righteousness" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

entries.title: Zechariah 8:9 "Let your hands be strong"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:9 "Let your hands be strong" This is a Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 304, KB 302) used in a JUSSIVE sense. Notice that this idiomatic phrase begins and concludes (cf. Zech. 8:13) this paragraph. This phrase shows the human side of the covenant relationship. This same kind of encouragement to faithful trust and steadfastness is found in Josh. 1:6-9; 1 Chr. 22:13; Isa. 35:4.

This may be an allusion to Haggai 2:4, who prophesied just before Zechariah. Both of them addressed the same issue—the rebuilding of the temple needs to be finished. Throughout Israel's history YHWH has encouraged His leaders and people to be strong and courageous and not to fear (e.g., Josh. 1:6-9; 1 Chr. 22:13; Isa. 35:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

entries.title: Zechariah 8:10
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:10 This is a summary of what life in Palestine was like ("before those days") between the fall of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar II (586 B.C.) and the return ("but now" of Zech. 8:11) to Jerusalem decreed by Cyrus II (538 B.C.).

The phrase "I set all men one against another" is the exact opposite of Zech. 8:3-8. YHWH's presence or absence can be noted by how people treat each other (cf. Zech. 7:8-14). We reap what we sow (cf. Gal. 6:7; and full list of all texts dealing with this subject). This is a recurrent theme in both the Old and New Testaments. Israel reaped the bounty of the presence and forgiveness of God (cf. Zech. 8:11-12).

Notice that YHWH takes personal responsibility for Israel and Judah's exile (cf. Zech. 8:14; 7:14). He allowed foreign nations to defeat His people (cf. Isa. 10:5; Jer. 13:9; 51:20). This judgment was the necessary discipline to bring about a renewed covenant and people. His judgment was a sign of His love (i.e., parental discipline).

entries.title: Zechariah 8:11 "the remnant"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:11 "the remnant" See note at Zech. 8:6 and SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses).

entries.title: Zechariah 8:12
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:12 This reflects the covenant blessings of Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29 (cf. Hag. 2:19).

entries.title: Zechariah 8:13
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:13 This is a very important verse because it shows the intended purpose of Israel. YHWH called Abraham to call a world (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6). His special relationship and blessing to the descendants of Abraham was meant to attract the notice of the rest of the sons of Adam. The nationalism of Genesis 10-11 is reflected in v. 10c. However, the Jewish people were not faithful to the covenant. Their lives did not reflect the holiness of YHWH, but the fallenness of Genesis 3. Those who were meant to be a light became a deterrent (cf. Ezek. 36:18-23). YHWH had to first change His own people's hearts and minds. They could not perform His covenant requirements. Therefore, a new covenant was required; one based on YHWH's character and provision (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:24-36). With this new covenant His people can become their intended "blessing" to a lost world.

The "curse" of Lev. 26 and Deut. 27-29 has been removed through the Messiah. The tragedy is that Israel did not recognize this new opportunity to fulfill her worldwide missionary mandate. She turned inward into exclusivism and pride instead of outward. YHWH's heart for "the nations" was not her heart. Monotheism and the unity of mankind (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) demands a universal people! Israel was a means to that end, not that end! The new age of righteousness depicted in Isaiah 55-66 was not fulfilled in the post-exilic return, but it will be in the Messianic Kingdom.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "Do not fear; let your hands be strong" These are both Qal IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense (cf. Zech. 8:9,15). This is a recurrent admonition. See note at v. 9.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:14 "I purposed"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:14 "I purposed" The VERB (BDB 273, KB 273, Qal PERFECT) is used in both v. 14 and v. 15.

  1. as YHWH "purposed" to judge His people because of their repeated covenant violations in the exiles of Assyria and Babylon
  2. now YHWH "purposed" to forgive and bless the returning exiled Jews (cf. v. 11)

YHWH is in control of history (i.e., Dan. 2:21). Covenant violations require a divine response (i.e., Lev. 26; Deut. 28). However, repentance and faithfulness bring divine blessing (i.e., "the two ways," cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Proverbs 1).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

▣ "I have not relented" The Hebrew VERB (BDB 636, KB 688), in its Niphal PERFECT stem originally referred to taking a deep breath. It came to refer to relief or sorrow (see a good brief word study in Robert Girdlestone, Synonyms of the OT, pp. 87-93). YHWH was patient with His people. He relented of the punishment that they deserved (cf. Amos 7:3,6), but there was a limit to His relenting (cf. Jer. 15:8). There came a time when YHWH disciplined His people and He did not relent (cf. Zech. 8:14; Ezek. 24:14), but He wanted to (cf. Jer. 26:3,13; Hosea 11:8).

This anthropomorphic word "relented" or "repented" shocks us because we think of God as unchangeable. It is surely true that His character and commitment to redemption are unchangeable, however, if God is unchangeable in all ways, why do we pray? Intercessory prayer is based on the belief that supplication can change God's dealings with humans, both individually and corporately. There is a true personal relationship between God and believers.

God's word is sure, both positively and negatively (e.g., Jer. 4:28; Ezek. 24:14; Gal. 6:7). God's faithless people finally reaped the consequences of their acts (cf. Zech. 7:9-14). God allowed exile to make restoration a possibility (cf. Zech. 8:15). God wants a people who reflect His character (cf. Zech. 8:8, 16-17; 7:9-10) so that the nations can know Him and trust Him!

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

entries.title: Zechariah 8:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:15 Judgment is YHWH's last resort. He wants to bless (e.g., Hosea 11:8) to fulfill His larger redemptive purposes (i.e., to restore all humans made in His image into fellowship with their Creator).

entries.title: Zechariah 8:16-17 "These are the things which you should do"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:16-17 "These are the things which you should do" These verses reflect Zech. 7:9-10 and 8:8, but they truly reflect the Mosaic legislation. It was very clear to these Jewish people what YHWH's two-pronged will for them was among each other and foreigners (i.e. two positive commands in Zech. 8:16 and two negative commands in 8:17).

This ethical aspect to biblical faith is needed in a day like theirs and ours when faith in God is limited to:

  1. initial decision (ticket to heaven)
  2. emotional moment
  3. selected times and places
  4. rituals/liturgy

These things are good, but unless they issue in a daily, moral lifestyle they are false hopes (cf. Matthew 7; John 15; 2 Peter 2). The goal of biblical faith is not only heaven when we die, but Christlikeness now (cf. Matt. 5:48; Rom. 8:28-30; 1 Cor. 3:18; Gal. 4:19; Eph. 1:6; 4:13; 1 Thess. 3:13; 4:3; 5:23; 1 Pet. 1:15). Anything less is biblically suspect! Western Christianity is characterized by "what is in it for me?" but true biblical faith is meant to serve and reflect God!

▣ "gates" This was the place of judicial acts and social events. For a good discussion of Israel's judicial system, see Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 152-155.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:17
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:17 The first two negated VERBS are Qal IMPERFECTS used in a JUSSIVE sense. YHWH hates premeditated schemes (i.e., Ps. 36:4; Prov. 3:29; 12:2; 14:22; Jer. 4:14; Micah 2:1; Zech. 7:10)!

▣ "all these are what I hate" Both

  1. "hate" (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal PERFECT, cf. Prov. 6:16-19)
  2. "love" (BDB 12, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense and the Qal IMPERATIVE, Zech. 8:19)

are human emotions applied to God (anthropomorphism, see SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN)

God is surely personal and thereby has feelings and emotions, but His holy, gracious, unchanging character controls the mood swings experienced by fallen humans. These words are analogous, not definitive!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

entries.title: Zechariah 8:19
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:19 This literary unit begins in Zech. 7:1 with a question about the need to continue certain fast days related to the Babylonian exile. After discussing the reason for the exile and the hope of restoration, Zechariah returns to the question about specific fast days.

▣ "The fast of the fourth" This was a fast in memory of Jerusalem's walls being breached (cf. Jer. 39:2; 2 Kgs. 25:3).

▣ "the fast of the fifth" This was a fast in memory of the destruction of the temple (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:8).

▣ "the fast of the seventh" This was a fast in memory of Gedaliah's death (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:25).

▣ "the fast of the tenth" This was a fast in memory of the beginning of Nebuchadnezzar II's siege of Jerusalem (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:1-2; Jer. 39:1).

▣ "will become joy, gladness, and cheerful feasts" There will be no more fasts! Israel's mourning will be changed to joy, her captivity into deliverance (cf. Jer. 31:10-14). Isaiah 65 combines a renewed Jerusalem with the New Age!

▣ "so love truth and peace" This is a summary statement of how repentant, restored, faithful followers should live (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL). Love is more than an emotion! It is an action (i.e., Jesus' two great commandments).

The phrase is similar to the Shema of Deut. 6:4-6. Eternal life has observable characteristics.

"Truth" is from the root (BDB 52, KB 63) which denotes faithfulness; see SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS).

"Peace" is both an attitude toward life and others as well as a wish that all can participate in it. See SPECIAL TOPIC: PEACE (shalom).

True faith is lived out among one's peers, community, and kin!

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed)

entries.title: Zechariah 8:20-21
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 8:20-21 As some came (possibly from Bethel (cf. Zech. 7:2) to seek the favor of the Lord, so now other cities of Judah come to Jerusalem and the new temple to seek YHWH's blessing.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:21 "to seek the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:21 "to seek the Lord" There are two parallel phrases:

  1. "to entreat the favor of" ‒ Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 318 II, KB 316
  2. "to seek" ‒ Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, BDB 134, KB 152

The VERB "seek" (BDB 134, KB 152, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) is used twice in vv. 21-22. It is a powerful VERB of action. Seeking YHWH implies a desire to know Him and follow Him. It denotes a sense of spiritual need as well as YHWH's desire to be found by humans made in His image and likeness.

  1. seek the face of YHWH ‒ 1 Sam. 21:1
  2. seek HIs face ‒ Ps. 105:4
  3. seek YHWH ‒ Exod. 33:7; Deut. 4:29; 1 Chr. 16:10; 2 Chr. 11:16; Prov. 28:5; Isa. 51:1; Jer. 50:4; Hosea 3:5; 5:6; Zeph. 1:6; 2:3
  4. seek Me ‒ 2 Chr. 15:2,4; Ps. 78:34; Isa. 45:19,22; 55:6; Jer. 29:13

Notice in this context all humans may come and worship YHWH!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "I will also go" This is an emphatic statement of intent (two COHORTATIVE forms of "go," cf. Zech. 8:23). There is an urgency to Zech. 8:21.

entries.title: Zechariah 8:22 "So many peoples and mighty nations will come"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
8:22 "So many peoples and mighty nations will come" The Hebrew ADJECTIVE "mighty" (BDB 783) can mean "numerous" (cf. Ps. 35:18; Prov. 7:26; Isa. 53:12; Amos 5:12). If so, then "many peoples" is parallel to "numerous nations."

As other Jews come so now the initial purpose of YHWH is fulfilled when "many peoples and mighty nations" come to Him (i.e., 1 Kgs. 8:43,60). This universal aspect in Zechariah (cf. Zech. 2:11) is surprising in light of

  1. Zech. 1:15,21
  2. the racial tone of Haggai
  3. the problems faced by Nehemiah (cf. Neh. 4:6)

Zechariah is looking beyond the immediate (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 56:7; 66:18-24; Micah 4:1-3). He is looking to the days of "the wounded shepherd" (cf. Zechariah, chapters 12-13)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

8:23
NASB  "will grasp the garment of a Jew"
NKJV  "will grasp the sleeve of a Jewish man"
NRSV  "shall take hold of a Jew, grasping his garment"
TEV  "come to one Jew"
NJB  "will take a Jew by the sleve"
JPSOA  "they will take hold of every Jew by a corner of his cloak"
Peshitta  "shall take hold of the skirt of a Jew"
NIV  "will take firm hold of one Jew by the hem of his robe"

The Hebrew VERB "take hold" (BDB 304, KB 302) in the Hiphil stem is repeated twice (first IMPERFECT then PERFECT with waw) for emphasis and urgency (see use in 1 Kgs. 1:50; 2:28; 2 Kgs. 4:27; Prov. 26:17; Isa. 4:1). In the ANE this was a gesture of submission or supplication.

The intended purpose of the call of Abraham (cf. Gen. 12:3) is to be realized!

The confusion (many languages) of the tower of Babel has now been overcome. The beginning of the church at Pentecost (cf. Acts 2) is the reversal of Genesis 10-11, as these people from many lands heard the gospel in their own language. This verse is a prophetic glimpse.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPEAKING IN TONGUES

SPECIAL TOPIC: JEWS

▣ "we have heard that God is with you" YHWH's presence is the greatest blessing (cf. Isa. 7:14; 8:8,10; 45:14) and the goal of creation (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8-9). This was what Israel was meant to convey to the nations! The barrier (cf. Gen. 3:10-21) between Him and mankind is removed.

"God" is Elohim; see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Why is there a lapse of time between Zech. 1:1 and Zech. 7:1?
  2. Who does Zech. 7:2 refer to?
  3. Why was God so upset with their religious fasts?
  4. What is the ultimate purpose of Israel?
  5. Why is Zech. 8:20-23 so surprising, yet so important?
