entries.title: Zechariah 14:1
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:1 This is a summary of the entire chapter which emphasizes YHWH's fighting on behalf of His people. In this chapter His people are depicted as ancient Israel. YHWH judged them and dispersed them, but now He restores their losses (cf. Isa. 53:12) and their place (i.e., Promised Land).

▣ "a day is coming for the Lord" The "day of the Lord" is a common theme of Zechariah 12-14, but this phrase has an added Hebrew PREPOSITION "of" (BDB 750 #5), which denotes that the day is His day!

The VERB (BDB 97, KB 112, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE) denotes an approach or arrival. YHWH will be publicly acknowledged as King and victor (cf. Zech. 14:9; 1 Cor. 15:24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE LAST DAYS

▣ "you" This is FEMININE SINGULAR referring to Jerusalem (cf. Zech. 14:2).

entries.title: Zechariah Contextual Insights
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
ZECHARIAH 14

PARAGRAPH DIVISIONS OF MODERN TRANSLATIONS

NASB NKJV NRSV TEV NJB
God Will Battle Jerusalem's Foes The Day of the Lord The Final Warfare and the Final Victory Jerusalem and the Nations The Eschatological Battle; the Splendor of Jerusalem
14:1-5 14:1-2 14:1-5 14:1-5 14:1-5
  14:3-7      
14:6-7   14:6-7 14:6-7 14:6-11
14:8 14:8-11 14:8 14:8-9  
God Will Be King Over All        
14:9-11   14:9    
    14:10-11 14:10-11  
14:12-15 14:12-15 14:12-15 14:12 14:12-15
      14:13-14  
  The Nations Worship the King   14:15  
14:16-19 14:16-19 14:16-19 14:16-19 14:16-19
14:20-21 14:20-21 14:20-21 14:20-21 14:20-21

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

  1. There have been many interpretations of this chapter. There are two Coming Ones.
    1. to take it very literally as referring to a future national Israel (dispensationalism)
    2. to spiritualize it to fit the current church exclusively (covenant theologians)
    3. to see it fulfilled in the destruction of Jerusalem in A.D. 70 by Rome (Steve Gregg, YouTube video on Zechariah 14)

  2. We must assert that this section, Zechariah 9-14, is very Messianic. As Zechariah 1-8 are quoted most often by John in the Revelation, so Zechariah 9-14 are quoted most often in the Gospels. Yet, the entire book points toward the end-time. It seems that the OT authors used past and current events to overshadow future events. When the last generation comes I think that this prophecy and all prophecy will be more easily understood.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

  3. Although, as historical-grammatical interpreters, we look closely at the text, we must remember that Christ is the focus of the OT. These passages are very Messianic, even though the historical setting is ambiguous. The NT is the proper interpreter of the OT. Christ is the ultimate, final revelation.
     I have been impressed by a partial preterist named Steve Gregg, (www.thenarrowpath.com) by his understanding that this chapter is about Israel's defeat by Rome in A.D. 66-70. I hope you will look at his YouTube videos on Zechariah 13 and 14.

  4. It is obvious that YHWH is still involved in national Israel. Their repentance and faith is coming (cf. Zech. 12:10; Romans 9-11). The Church, in many ways, has supplemented, complemented, and fulfilled Israel's initial task, which was to be a kingdom of priests to bring all humans to a knowledge of YHWH so that they may be saved through the Messiah (cf. Gen. 3:15; 12:3; 18:18; Exod. 19:4-6; I Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6).

  5. Be careful of being too dogmatic concerning your personal interpretation. Often we are overly influenced by theories or systematic theologies which are current in our day.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

  6. Zechariah 14 is a picture of the sons of God's victory in history (cf. Rev. 11:15). It is not as Messianic as Zechariah 10-13. The Father is the focus and the ideal age is the setting. However, OT functions, as well as titles for God, are transferred to the Son. This apocalyptic literature is an idealized future scene in terms of ancient Israel's capital.
    SPECIAL TOPIC: APOCALYPTIC LITERATURE

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

entries.title: Zechariah 14:2 "For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem to battle"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:2 "For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem to battle" Notice the emphasis is on YHWH's control of history (cf. Zech. 14:9; 12:2,3,6,9; Ps. 2; Isa. 8:9-10; 17:12-14; Ezek. 38-39; Joel 3:9-17; Rev. 16:14-16; 19:17-19).

▣ "the city will be captured" The VERB (BDB 539, KB 530, Niphil PERFECT with waw) reflects the final, ultimate confrontation between the kingdoms of this world and the kingdom of our God will result in the partial fall of Jerusalem (cf. Zech. 13:8). This fall is described in vivid terms from Jerusalem's past experience with conquering invaders. However, a remnant will remain (in Zech. 13:8 only 1/3, but here 1/2). This is a stark contrast to the divine protection promised in Zech. 12:1-9.

SPECIAL TOPIC: REMNANT (three senses)

entries.title: Zechariah 14:3
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:3 YHWH fights on behalf of His people as He did in the exodus from Egypt and the conquest and settlement of Canaan.

In an eschatological sense YHWH is depicted as once-and-for-all fighting on behalf of His people and setting up a new order.

  1. Psalm 2; Isa. 2:2-4; Ezekiel 38-39; Zechariah 14
  2. in intertestamental, apocalyptic literature, I Enoch 56:5-8 and IV Ezra 13:1-13,25-53
  3. in the NT in Rev. 20:7-9

entries.title: Zechariah 14:4 "And in that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:4 "And in that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives" The PRONOUN anthropomorphically reflects YHWH (cf. "Lord" of Zech. 14:1,3,5 and PRONOUN of Zech. 14:2a). However, the Messiah often takes on the titles and functions of the Father. In context, this chapter is oriented toward the Father.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPHMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "the Mount of Olives will be split in its middle from east to west by a very large valley" The Mount of Olives is a 2½ mile ridge running to the east of Jerusalem and culminates in the city of Bethany. It is mentioned only here in the OT. Apparently this earth-shaking event will occur for two purposes:

  1. the return of the Lord to do battle for His people (v. 3)
  2. a way of escape for the remnant that are still left in the city (v. 5)
  3. the water of life to flow (cf. Zech. 14:8; 13:1; Ps. 46:4; Ezek. 47:1-12; Rev. 22:1)
14:5
NASB  "And you will flee by the valley of My mountain"
NKJV  "then you shall flee through My mountain valley"
NRSV  "and you shall flee by the valley of the Lord's mountain"
TEV  "You will escape through the valley that divides the mountain in two"
NJB  "the valley between the hills will be filled"
JPSOA, LXX  "And the valley of my mountains shall be blocked up"

There has been much confusion in the translation of this verse. The word "flee" occurs three times in Zech. 14:5 (BDB 630, KB 681, Qal PERFECTS), but the ancient translations fluctuate the translation from "flee" to "you shall be stopped" (BDB 711).

The Masoretic Text is followed by the Peshitta and the Vulgate, while the Septuagint and Symmachus' translation follow the Aramaic Targums.

The UBS Text Project, p. 422, gives the MT (NASB) a "C" rating (considerable doubt) to the first occurrence of the VERB "flee" (BDB 630, KB 681, Qal PERFECT with waw), but to the second occurrence it gives a "B" rating.

The difference between "and you will flee" and "it will be blocked" is only vowel points. The context favors the MT because it is a context of restoration and abundance, not judgment. YHWH comes to deliver.

▣
NASB  "Azel"
NKJV, NRSV, JPSOA  "Azal"
TEV   —
NJB  "Jasol"
REB  "Asal"
LXX  "Iasol"
Peshitta  "disaster"

This seems to refer to a city, possibly also mentioned in Micah 1:11 ("Beth-ezel"), which shows the terminus of this supernaturally-made valley (cf. NRSV).

▣ "the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah" Josephus (Antiq. 9.10.4) links it with 2 Chr. 26:16-23, when Uzziah offered a sacrifice and was struck with leprosy. This same earthquake is referred to in Amos 1:1 (i.e., 750 B.C.). This may imply that an earthquake will form the valley, but this is not a certainty. Earthquakes are used to describe YHWH's presence in judgment (cf. Isa. 29:6; Ezek. 38:19).

▣ "the Lord. . .will come and all the holy ones" This refers to YHWH's coming with angels (cf. Deut. 33:2-3). Angels are called holy ones in Job 5:1; 15:5; Ps. 89:5,7; Dan. 8:13.

The term "holy" is also used of believers in the OT (cf. Ps. 16:3; 34:9; Isa. 4:3; Dan. 7:18,21,22,25,27; 8:24).

In the NT it refers to Jesus' Second Coming and may include angels and believers (cf. Matt. 16:27; 25:31; Mark 8:38; 2 Thess. 1:7; Rev. 19:14).

▣ "with Him" The Masoretic Text has "with You," which may refer to Jerusalem (FEMININE SINGULAR, cf. Zech. 14:1).

14:6
NASB  "In that day there will be no light; the luminaries will dwindle"
NKJV  "there will be no light, the lights will diminish"
NRSV, REB  "on that day there shall not be either cold or frost"
TEV  "when the time comes, there will no longer be cold or frost"
NJB, Pehsitta  "that Day, there will be no light, but only cold and frost"
JPSOA  "In that day, there shall be neither sunlight no cold moon light"

The Septuagint and the Vulgate interpret the last phrase as "no cold and ice" (cf. New International Dictionary of Old Testament Theology and Exegesis, vol. 3, pp. 952, 995). However, the eschatological context may refer to the dwindling light (BDB 21) of the heavenly bodies (cf. Isa. 13:10; 24:23; 60:19; Jer. 4:23; Ezek. 32:7,8; Joel 2:31; 3:15; Matt. 24:29; Acts 2:19).

The second Hebrew phrase has two words: (1) "precious," "rare," "splendid," "weighty" (BDB 429) and (2) "thicken," "condense," "congeal" (BDB 891, KB 1117, Qal IMPERFECT). The NASB footnote has "glorious ones will congeal."

entries.title: Zechariah 14:7 "For it will be a unique day which is known to the Lord"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:7 "For it will be a unique day which is known to the Lord" The timing of this day relates to Matt. 24:36 and reenforces the understanding that this section refers to God the Father. The uniqueness may be that there is no more night (cf. TEV). All the normal aspects of creation are reversed. This will be a time of re-creation (i.e., 2 Pet. 3:7,10,12).

▣ "at evening time there will be light" YHWH's presence provides continual light (cf. Isa. 60:19,20; Rev. 21:25; 22:5), as it did before the creation of the sun, stars, and moon (cf. Gen. 1:3-5 versus 1:14-19).

entries.title: Zechariah 14:8 "living waters will flow out of Jerusalem"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:8 "living waters will flow out of Jerusalem" This seems to be used in the sense of life-giving, supernatural waters (cf. Gen. 2:10), which issue not only in physical bounty, but also in spiritual bounty. These waters are often referred to in the Bible (cf. Ps. 46:4; Isa. 33:21-23; 49:10; Ezek. 47:1-12; Joel 3:18; John 4:13-15; 6:35; 7:37-38; Rev. 22:1,2 and in a negative way in Jer. 2:13; Zech. 9:11). Jerusalem, because of YHWH's presence, is the center of all creation (similar to waters flowing from God into Eden). The King is enthroned there!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE WATERS

▣ "the eastern sea. . .the western sea" This refers to the Dead Sea (which will no longer be dead!) and the Mediterranean Sea.

▣ "it will be in summer as well as in winter" In Palestine there are really only two seasons. This verse implies continual water, which is not related to the seasonal changes. This whole context speaks of a new natural order which is not dependent on regular cycles of nature.

entries.title: Zechariah 14:9 "the Lord will be king"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:9 "the Lord will be king" This continues the motif of YHWH as King of the earth (cf. Zech. 14:16,17; 1 Sam. 8:7; 12:12; Ps. 93:1; 97:1; 99:1). In Zech. 9:9 it is the Messiah who is king (cf. Isa. 9:6-7; Jer. 10:7; 23:5). YHWH does not become King. He has always been King, but now all humans recognize it (cf. Matt. 6:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

▣ "over all the earth" Here is the continuing theme of the universal reign of YHWH (cf. Zech. 14:6; Ps. 22:27-28; 47:8-9; Isa. 2:2-4; 45:2-3). Jerusalem has become "the center," "the navel" of the created order (i.e., Isa. 2:2-4)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "in that day the Lord will be the only one, and His name the only one" This is an emphasis on monotheism (cf. Exod. 8:10; 9:14; Deut. 4:35,39; 6:4-5; 33:26; 1 Sam. 2:2; 2 Sam. 22:32; 1 Kgs. 8:23; Ps. 86:8; Isa. 46:9; Jer. 10:6-7.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

entries.title: Zechariah 14:10 "All the land will be changed into a plain from"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:10 "All the land will be changed into a plain from" This supernatural altering of the earth's terrain has been interpreted in several ways:

  1. as a theological symbol of the holiness of the area (i.e., the nation of Judah north to south)
  2. as universal access to the place where YHWH dwells (new Eden)
  3. as the equal distribution of this living water to all people (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

Some see an allusion to this topographical preparation in Isa. 40:4.

▣ "Geba" This is a city located six miles north of Jerusalem, which is mentioned in 2 Kgs. 23:8. Its name means "height." It was the northern boundary of Judah (cf. Josh. 18:24).

▣ "Rimmon south of Jerusalem" This village is mentioned several times in the OT (cf. Josh. 15:32; 19:7; and Neh. 11:29), but its exact location is uncertain. It was in the tribal allocation of Simeon. It is not the same as Rimmon mentioned in Josh. 19:13, which was in the tribal allocation of Zebulun.

▣ "Jerusalem will rise" This topological rising (BDB 926 or 910, KB 1163, Qal PERFECT with waw) of the city above its surrounding area was predicted by Isa. 2:2 and Micah 4:1, which are both eschatological passages that predict the nations will come in great numbers to YHWH in Jerusalem (cf. Zech. 8:20-23). Is this symbolic of access to YHWH or is it an actual physical modification of Judah? Other prophets speak of a completely new and permanent earth (cf. Isa. 65:17; 66:22). This tension is one reason (along with expecting all prophecies relating to Israel's geographical promises to be literally fulfilled) that many see an earthly kingdom (millennium, Rev. 20:1-6) before the eternal kingdom (cf. Dan. 7:13; Rev. 21-22). My problem is that no NT writer reaffirms these national, geographical promises to Israel. Jesus even asserts that true worship is not connected to any mountain (cf. John 4:20-26).

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY DO OT COVENANT PROMISES SEEM SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

▣ "and remain on its site" The VERB (BDB 442, KB 444) is a Qal PERFECT with waw. This verse is very specific. Although all of the sites and gates within the city are now uncertain, it is obvious that it refers to the entire city of Jerusalem. Jerusalem is secure (cf. Zech. 12:6; Jer. 30:18).

▣ "Benjamin's Gate" Mentioned in Jer. 37:13; 38:7, it is also known as the

  1. "Sheep Gate" (Neh. 3:1,32; 12:39) at the upper end of the east wall
  2. "Mustering Gate" (Neh. 3:31)
  3. "Upper Benjamin Gate" (Jer. 20:2)
  4. "North Gate of the Temple Court" (Ezek. 8:3)

It would have led to the north, to Jericho.

▣ "the First Gate" This gate is associated with the "Old Gate" (cf. Neh. 3:6; 12:39).

▣ "the Corner Gate" First mentioned in 2 Kgs. 14:13; 2 Chr. 25:23; 26:9, it is also mentioned in Jer. 31:38. It was located on the western hill.

▣ "the Tower of Hananel" This was located on the northeast, near the temple (cf. Neh. 3:1; 12:39; Jer. 31:38).

▣ "the king's wine presses" Probably in the king's garden area in the southern part of the city. (Neh. 3:15)

▣ The reason there is some confusion in identifying the location of these gates is because of the complete destruction of the city of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar II in 586 B.C. The restored city, by Cyrus II's decree in 538 B.C. was very small compared to the previous capital of Judah. The returnees were only able to re-wall a smaller diameter. Therefore, the restored gates were not in the same place but possibly in proximity.

However, these tower locations would reflect the whole city of Jerusalem from north to south and east to west.

entries.title: Zechariah 14:11 "And people will live in it, and there will be no more curse"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:11 "And people will live in it, and there will be no more curse" The curse mentioned may have several origins:

  1. the curse of Gen. 3:17, which is related to mankind's sin
  2. the curse of Deuteronomy 28, which is related to Israel's breaking the covenant (cf. Zech. 8:18 and Rev. 22:3)
  3. the curse of complete destruction (i.e., Jericho, cf. Josh. 6:17,21; Jer. 25:9)

It is obvious that Jerusalem will be densely populated, which was a change from the prevailing attitude of Zechariah's own day (cf. Neh. 7:4; 11:1-2).

This "no more curse" is picked up in Rev. 22:3.

▣ "for Jerusalem will dwell in security" This VERB (BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT with waw, #4) has the meaning of "abide in its place" (cf. Zech. 2:8; 9:5; 14:11; Lev. 26:5; Jer. 23:6; Ezek. 28:26; 34:25-31; 38:8). They are secure (BDB 105) and dwell in the land because YHWH and His Messiah (cf. Isa. 7:14) dwell with them!

entries.title: Zechariah 14:12 "Now this will be the plague"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:12 "Now this will be the plague" YHWH will defeat the nations (cf. Zech. 14:2-3) by a means (i.e., a plague, BDB 620) which He had employed earlier in His defense of Jerusalem against Sennacherib in 701 B.C. (cf. 2 Kgs. 19:35; Isa. 37:36). This may be a reference to Deut. 28:20-24, which is now turned against Israel's enemies (e.g., Deut. 28:7; Ps. 89:22-24).

▣ "the Lord will strike" This VERB (BDB 619, KB 669, Qal IMPERFECT) is often used of YHWH's defense of His people (but there are exceptions, cf. Exod. 21:22; Ps. 91:12; Prov. 3:23).

entries.title: Zechariah 14:13 "a great panic from the Lord will fall on them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:13 "a great panic from the Lord will fall on them" This is another supernatural means whereby the army of the nations will fall. They will simply destroy themselves (cf. Exod. 15:16; 23:27; Jdgs. 7:22; 1 Sam. 14:15-20; 2 Chr. 20:22-23; Hag. 2:22). Confusion (BDB 223) of the enemies of YHWH is part of the Day of the Lord (cf. Deut. 7:23; 28:20; Isa. 22:5).

This imagery is part of Holy War (i.e., the Conquest) terminology. YHWH is fighting on behalf of His people!

14:14;
NASB, LXX, NET  "Judah will fight at Jerusalem"
NKJV, Peshitta  "Judah also will fight at Jerusalem"
NRSV  "even Judah will fight at Jerusalem"
NJB  "even Judah will fight against Jerusalem"
REB  "Judah too will fight at Jerusalem"
TEV  "The men of Judah will fight to defend Jerusalem"
JPSOA  "Judah shall join the fighting in Jerusalem"

Grammatical features:

  1. The VERB (BDB 535, KB 526) is a Niphil IMPERFECT.
  2. The PREPOSITION "at" (i.e., place) is also used in the NIV, while the RSV changes it to "against" (cf. Vulgate, Targums). The same PRONOUN is translated "against" in Zech. 14:3.

The context implies that Judah will fight with Jerusalem!

▣ "the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered" The VERB (BDB 62, KB 74) is a Pual PERFECT. See Zech. 14:1.

entries.title: Zechariah 14:15
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:15 This information seems out of place. It should go with the plague on humans mentioned in Zech. 14:12. It seems to refer to the complete destruction of this invading army's military capabilities.

entries.title: Zechariah 14:16 "any who are left of all the nations that went against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:16 "any who are left of all the nations that went against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts" This magnifies the eternal redemptive plan of God. This could mean

  1. that some few soldiers survived
  2. that some from the nations survived, but those of the nations who are left will be converted (cf. Zech. 8:20-23)!

There is an allusion to the world-wide annual worship in Isa. 2:2-4 (cf. Isa. 66:19-24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "to celebrate the Feast of Booths" This feast is described in Lev. 23:34-44 and Deut. 16:13-17. Foreigners were welcome to participate (cf. Deut. 16:14). It was basically a time for

  1. thanksgiving for the harvest
  2. God's provision for the poor
  3. a time for reading the Torah (cf. Neh. 8:14-18)

The mention of living waters in Zech. 8:14 and their use in John 7, during the Feast of Tabernacles (Booths), seems to be significant. During the Feast of Tabernacles several ceremonies pointed toward this living water as a symbol of spiritual strength.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL

entries.title: Zechariah 14:17-19 "there will be no rain on them"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content: 14:17-19 "there will be no rain on them" All of the remaining pagans seem to be converted to faith in YHWH at this eschatological period. Any who refuse to come and worship at least annually are cursed with the plague of Deut. 28:22-24. Egypt had seen the plagues of YHWH before! It is surprising that some nations may not come. It is possible to interpret this as "not everyone is fully converted to faith in Christ." Some see this as characteristic of the millennium of Rev. 20:1-6.

entries.title: Zechariah 14:20,21 "In that day there will be inscribed. . .'HOLY TO THE Lord'"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:20,21 "In that day there will be inscribed. . .'HOLY TO THE Lord'" These two verses describe human society that has now become entirely sanctified and holy. This can be seen by the insignia which was originally on the turban of Aaron, the high priest (cf. Exod. 28:36), and now on the eschatological High Priest (cf. Zech. 3:9, is also on the common things and people). The different aspects of society which were affected are

  1. the bells of the horses
  2. the cooking pots in the Lord's house
  3. the cooking pots in the homes of the people of Jerusalem and Judea (who are now partakers of the holy food of the temple; joint heirs with the Levites and priests)

entries.title: Zechariah 14:21 "And there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts in that day"
entries.author: Dr. Bob Utley
entries.content:
14:21 "And there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts in that day" The term "Canaanite" (NASB, NKJV, NIV) can refer to any unholy person not included in the covenant people, but there should not be any of these remaining. Therefore, many translators interpret this term as "merchant" (BDB 489 II, i.e., one who weighs out gold and silver, cf. Prov. 31:24; Isa. 23:8; Ezek. 16:29; 17:4; Hosea 12:7) and this is how it is used in the NT of money changers and sellers in the court of the Gentiles in the temple (cf. Matt. 21:12-13; Mark 11:15-17; Luke 19:45-46; John 2:13-16).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

  1. Will this chapter be fulfilled literally or symbolically? Why?
  2. Is this chapter apocalyptic literature and if so, what does that imply in its interpretation?
  3. Relate the significant themes of Zechariah 12-14 and compare them with a reference Bible throughout the Old Testament.
  4. Is this chapter Messianic or YHWH oriented? Why?
  5. How and why is Zechariah's prophecy so influential on NT writers?
